Cloud microservice architectures often experience temporary miscoordination that leads to system overloads, causing the rejection of valuable transactions and triggering harmful retry storms. To address this issue, researchers propose DiffTry (Differential Retries), a lightweight, distributed mechanism that assigns different retry limits to requests based on their priority class. By granting more retry attempts to high-priority transactions, DiffTry effectively transforms standard retry operations into a rejection prioritization system without requiring explicit overload detection or service coordination. The authors developed a comprehensive analytical model to quantify these prioritization and rejection rates across both single services and complex networks. Finally, simulations and real-world deployments on Kubernetes confirm that DiffTry successfully protects critical traffic from incidental and adversarial overloads while seamlessly integrating as a drop-in plugin.

The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is issuing a direct final rule to update its Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) regulations based on statutory amendments passed in 2021 and 2023. The rule broadens FMLA eligibility by allowing virtually all Federal civilian service and certain honorable active military service to count toward the 12-month qualifying service requirement. It also clarifies that employees may substitute annual or sick leave earned under non-title 5 authorities for unpaid FMLA leave. Additionally, the rule excludes certain Veterans Health Administration employees from title 5 FMLA coverage because they are governed by a separate, VA-specific leave system. Because Paid Parental Leave requires FMLA eligibility, these updates directly impact parental leave access, and the rule will take effect on December 14, 2026, unless significant adverse comments are received.
